carmen: Onboarding request: axion-13b -> need a quick runtime compatibility triage before we promote to staging. Focus areas: RoPE scaling/offsets, KV-cache layout & dtype, and quantization (q4/gptq) experiments. Starting thread so we can checklist and assign.

josh_dev: Can you paste the HF model link + config? also any notes on attention implementation (flash/standard) and pos-emb? :eyes:

carmen: Link: https://huggingface.co/axion/axion-13b-final
Config excerpt:
```
"hidden_size": 8192,
"num_attention_heads": 64,
"rotary_emb": true,
"rope_base": 10000,
"rope_scaling": "linear",
"kv_cache_format": "b,s,h,d",
"attention_impl": "flash_attn"
```

mikayla_ml: Important — rope_scaling=linear means the model was trained with RoPE extrapolation. Runtime needs RoPE offset support (for chunked decoding) or we'll see degraded coherency at long contexts. Quick question: does the checkpoint include rotary_scale params or are they baked into weights?

carmen: The ckpt has no explicit scale tensor; scaling behavior is in training code. So runtime must apply scaled_rope math with base=10000 and linear schedule.

ryan_infra: KV cache mismatch alert: HF config says kv_cache_format=b,s,h,d while our runtime expects b,h,s,d. That affects how we memcpy/reshape caches between model steps. If we naively treat it as b,h,s,d we'll end up with scrambled heads. We need an adapter in the kernel to transpose on load or update runtime to accept both layouts.
josh_dev: Agreed. Implementing a one-time reshape in model loader should be fine but watch memory transient costs. Can we do an in-place reinterpretation for fp16?
neha_research: Proposed quick tests to gate bring-up (small checklist):
- parity inference vs fp16 baseline on 1000 prompts (token-level match / logprobs)
- perplexity on wikitext-2 and a held-out Redwood eval set
- long-context coherence test (2k -> 16k) for RoPE scaling
- attention-head-signature diff: compare attention matrices aggregated over 100 prompts
- quantization sweep: q8_0, q4_0, gptq-4-bit (group sizes 128/64) with RMSE and downstream evals

Here's a quick script we can run as a job (rough):
```bash
python tools/model_parity.py --model hf://axion/axion-13b-final --baseline fp16 --prompts data/short_prompts.jsonl --out /tmp/axion_parity.jsonl
```

eval-bot: automated-quant-results: finished q-sweep on small sample (100 prompts). Results (quality measured by avg BLEU-like scoring vs fp16 baseline):
- float16 baseline: 0.0 drop
- q8_0: -0.6
- q4_0: -2.3
- gptq-4bit(gs=128): -1.1
- gptq-4bit(gs=64): -0.9
Latency (tokens/sec) on p4d-like instance:
- fp16: 124 t/s
- q8_0: 156 t/s
- q4_0: 212 t/s
Notes: q4_0 gives best perf but largest quality delta; GPTQ variants trade quality for some perf.

josh_dev: For RoPE we may need to add a flag to the rotary kernel to apply linear scaling with offset support (optionally different math path for chunked vs full-context). I'll sketch patch to kernel with unit tests. :thumbsup:

ryan_infra: Ops/rollout requirements: place axion-13b behind a canary with automatic fallback to axion-6b (or axion-13b-fp16) if latency p50 > 2x baseline or error rate spike > 2%. Also add a runtime config entry 'kv_layout' so we don't rely on implicit layouts.
mikayla_ml: I'll run attention-heatmap diffs and head-wise cosine similarity test today and post plots. If we see head permutation issues that confirms cache transpose bug.
neha_research: On quantization: recommend running gptq with group size 64 and per-channel scales for matmuls. If we still see >1% downstream degradation, mark q4_0 as experimental and use q8_0 as default.
carmen: Summary/todo:
- [josh_dev] patch rotary kernel for rope_scaling+offset support (ETA EOD)
- [josh_dev] loader adapter to transpose kv cache if HF format != runtime format
- [mikayla_ml] attention/head-sim tests + plots (ETA today)
- [neha_research] full quant sweep on 1000 prompts + GPTQ runs (ETA 48h)
- [ryan_infra] add kv_layout runtime param + canary fallback policy to deploy config
- [eval-bot] run parity & perf jobs and post a follow-up thread with CSVs

josh_dev: Also callout: flash_attn vs non-flash — if flash implemented differently across kernels we need to ensure our fused attention respects RoPE math. If not, fallback to non-flash attention path for axion until validated.

ryan_infra: I'll add a quick incident playbook entry to roll back model variants and to hotfix cache transpose if needed.

mikayla_ml: posted initial head-sim plots in #eng-ml-artifacts (link) — early sign of head order mismatch in token positions 1..16. cc @ryan_infra

carmen: Great. If everyone can ack on their tasks I'll move this to "onboarding: in progress" and create a tracking issue with checklist. Thanks all. :party_parrot:
